summaryTab.matchCommentary:
The Test match at Kensington Oval commenced with high tactical intensity as West Indies posted 289/10 (101.3 ov) in their opening innings. In response, England countered with 77/10 (30.2 ov), setting the stage for a compelling contest of tactical endurance. Early sessions tested batting resolve against disciplined seam movement, with both attacks striving to gain the upper hand on a developing surface.

The defining turning point arrived during Century: JO Holder 202 (229b), which irrevocably altered the trajectory of the match. As the match progressed through its pivotal middle stages, JO Holder delivered a masterclass for West Indies (207 Runs & 2 Wkts), absorbing intense pressure and tilting the momentum decisively. Crucial partnership stands and incisive bowling spells broke the opposition's resistance, shifting the control share (West Indies 51%) and allowing West Indies to dictate terms heading into the decisive sessions.

Entering the final innings, England faced an uphill battle under unrelenting scoreboard pressure. West Indies's bowling unit, bolstered by RL Chase (54 Runs & 8 Wkts), maintained relentless discipline and attacked the stumps relentlessly. Wicket clusters in the closing sessions dismantled any remaining resistance, sealing West Indies won by 381 runs in comprehensive fashion.

Verdict: West Indies's triumph was built on superior pressure absorption, clinical execution during critical moments, and the ability to dominate key sessions. While England produced fighting phases, West Indies won the pivotal turning points and sustained higher tactical control across all five days to emerge as deserved victors.
